Encode Residue Environments and Graph Distances

fp_residue_pair.Rd

Computes a fixed-size hashed fingerprint of unordered residue pairs using their endpoint environments and shortest glycosidic-edge distance.

Usage

fp_residue_pair(
  glycans,
  ...,
  radius = 1L,
  n_bits = 2048L,
  mode = "binary",
  na_action = "propagate"
)

Arguments

glycans

A glyrepr::glycan_structure() vector or a character vector in any format supported by glyparse::auto_parse(). Formats are detected automatically, as in glymotif. For explicit format selection, use the corresponding glyparse parser first. Structures must be complete: concrete residues, specified linkages, positions, substituents and reducing-end alpha/beta state. Unknown or ambiguous fields raise an error.

...

Reserved for future options. Must be empty.

radius

Radius of each endpoint's WL environment, an integer from 0 to 10. The default 1 captures immediate neighbors and linkage labels. Only the final radius is used for endpoints, not all intermediate radii.

n_bits

Number of fixed hash bins, an integer from 1 to 1048576. The default 2048 balances vector size and folding collisions; it is not optimized for a particular prediction task.

mode

"binary" (default) records occupied bins; "count" sums feature occurrences, including repeated environments and collisions in each bin.

na_action

"propagate" (default) returns an all-NA vector for each missing input; "error" rejects missing inputs.

Value

A list of named integer vectors of length n_bits, preserving input length, order and names. Missing inputs yield all-NA vectors, a single residue yields all zeros, and empty input yields list().

Details

Every distinct unordered residue pair contributes one feature consisting of the lexically sorted endpoint labels and their undirected shortest-path length. Endpoints use the same residue labels, root information and directed linkage messages as fp_circular_binary(). All distances are included; there is no cutoff. Distance is a number of glycosidic edges, not a 3D or spatial distance.

A count vector sums to n * (n - 1) / 2 for n residues. There are no self-pairs: a single-residue glycan yields an all-zero vector and cannot be distinguished from another single residue with this method. Use fp_circular_binary() or motif features when that distinction matters.

Endpoint environments can preserve local linkage and anomer information, but the feature does not record the sequence of residues or linkages along the intervening path beyond those environments. With radius = 0, even linkage acceptor positions are omitted. Pair histograms are not complete graph invariants. Large glycans require quadratic pair enumeration and an all-pairs distance matrix. This residue-level design is inspired by atom-pair features; it is not an implementation of atom-level atom pairs or MAP4.

Fixed hashing and collisions

Fields are UTF-8 strings prefixed by their byte lengths. Full SHA-256 digests encode WL labels and method-specific features. The first 32 bits of each final digest, interpreted big-endian, are reduced modulo n_bits to select a bin. Colliding features add their counts or share a binary bit. There is no random seed, learned vocabulary, or batch-dependent dictionary. Distinct structures can share a fingerprint because of feature loss or collisions; equality is not proof of isomorphism. Larger n_bits reduces folding collisions but does not restore missing structural information. Bin names encode method, version, radius, dimension and mode. Compare vectors only under identical settings and compatible package/dependency versions. Counts are occurrence counts, not counts of unique subgraphs. No torch runtime or model weights are used.

Complete structures

All fingerprint functions validate complete input structures. Missing inputs are distinct from unknown structure fields: empty input returns list() and missing inputs retain the full coordinate set filled with NA values. Recompute compared vectors when the model, dictionary or implementation changes.

References

Carhart, Smith and Venkataraghavan (1985). Atom pairs as molecular features in structure-activity studies: definition and applications. doi:10.1021/ci00046a002 .

See also

fp_circular_binary(), fp_motif_count(), fp_motif_binary()

Examples

x <- c("Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc(b1-", "Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc(b1-4)GlcNAc(b1-")
fp <- fp_residue_pair(x, mode = "count")
vapply(fp, sum, 0)
#> [1] 1 3
identical(fp_residue_pair(x[1], mode = "count"), fp[1])
#> [1] TRUE
